title: Five smooth stones (1 Samuel 17)
hookLine: a shepherd refuses the king's armor and faces a giant
last: THE LORD LOOKS AT THE HEART.

lines: A BOY BRINGS BREAD TO HIS BROTHERS.
cards: Two armies face each other across a valley, and for forty days nobody moves. Every morning and every evening, a champion walks out from the Philistine side and shouts: send me one man. If he beats me, we'll serve you.
Goliath of Gath. Huge, in a bronze helmet and a coat of mail, with a spear like a weaver's beam. And every morning Israel's army, King Saul included, stays put, afraid.
Then Jesse's youngest son shows up from Bethlehem with grain and loaves for his older brothers. He hears the shouting and asks: who is this, to defy the armies of the living God?

teach.b: David offers to fight. Saul says what anyone would: you're a boy, and he's been a warrior since his youth. David answers with his résumé: I keep my father's sheep.
When a lion or a bear took a lamb, I went after it. The Lord who saved me from the lion will save me from this Philistine.

So Saul says go, and kindly dresses David in his own armor, a bronze helmet, a coat of mail, the king's sword. David clanks a few steps and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "I cannot go thus, for I am not used to it."

teach.h: A STAFF, A SLING, FIVE STONES.
teach.b: Instead he picks up his staff, a sling, and "five smooth stones out of the brook," dropped into his shepherd's bag. Tools he knows. Goliath sees a young man with a stick and is insulted: am I a dog?

teach.h: IN THE NAME OF THE LORD OF HOSTS.
teach.b: David's answer is the center of the story: "Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts." One stone, slung, and the giant falls on his face.
The story is about trust: the battle is the Lord's, David says, not won by sword and spear.
And it's about being yourself. Saul's armor was a gift, kindly meant; it just wasn't his. David doesn't win as a smaller copy of Saul.
He fights as a shepherd, with a shepherd's things, and that's enough.

how: Catholics hear the story of David and Goliath in the weekday Mass readings, and Catholic schools and youth programs tell it as a story of trusting God and using the gifts you've been given.

s: David refused Saul's armor because it was too big
the text says he wasn't used to it: I cannot go thus, for I am not used to it.
David picked up five stones but used only one
one stone, slung, struck the Philistine in the forehead.

he said the Lord saves not with sword and spear, for the battle is the Lord's.

games.q: you're David. King Saul has just dressed you in his own helmet, mail and sword for the fight. you can barely walk. what do you do?
o: keep it on; it's the king's armor.
take it off, and pick up your sling and five stones.
ask for a smaller set of armor.
games.why: he takes it all off: "I cannot go thus, for I am not used to it." he goes out with a staff, a sling and five smooth stones, in the name of the Lord.

practice: Think of your own giant, and notice whose armor you've been wearing for it: a boss's style, a parent's way with conflict, someone online who seems to have it figured out.
Take it off, then name your five smooth stones: patience, humor, a skill you practiced alone for years, a friend you trust. If you pray, bring your giant to God.

wordCard.voice: Goliath. The giant David faced with a shepherd's sling and stones from the brook, instead of the king's armor, in the name of the Lord. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: stone. David chooses five smooth stones from the stream for his shepherd's bag.

carryVoice: Your line: not in borrowed armor. The battle is the Lord's, not the armor's. See you tomorrow.
